hook.text: A local newspaper closes. Within two years, corruption in the town government doubles. No one is watching anymore.

buildup.text: Quality journalism costs money — investigative reporting requires time, expertise, and legal support.

discovery.text: Audiences who demand free content but also demand quality journalism are asking for something the market can't sustain.

twist.text: Subscribing, donating, and paying for journalism is not charity. It's investing in the infrastructure of democracy.

climax.text: When newsrooms close, accountability disappears. The public pays for free news with worse governance.

punchline.text: Free news isn't free. Someone always pays. If not you, then democracy does.

quiz.question: What happens when local newspapers close?
options: Government accountability decreases and corruption tends to increase
